title: Annotatio VI §.II Classis I.2: 1 Cor 10:21 — demon-communion excludes Christ
pass_a_gloss: Whence follows the second argument of the first class, interpretive and confirming of the Institution History concerning Judas the impious Guest, plainly incapable of communion with Christ because of his destined impiety — the Apostolic word that those fostering Communion with Devils (such as the Apostle John testifies falls on all the impious: 1 Jn 1:6; 3:6, 8, 9) are excluded from every possibility of communion with Christ (1 Cor 10:21): You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot be partakers of the Lord’s Table and of the table of demons.
pass_b_english: Class I, argument 2 confirms the Judas history from the Apostles: those who keep communion with demons are shut out from any communion with Christ.
John marks that state in all the impious (1 Jn 1:6; 3:6, 8–9); Paul: you cannot drink the Lord’s cup and demons’ cup, or share the Lord’s table and demons’ table (1 Cor 10:21).
source_text: Unde sequitur alterum primæ classis argumentum, Historiæ Institutionis S. Cœnæ, de Juda Conviva impio, & ob impietatem suam destinatam, communionis cum Christo planè incapaci, interpretativum ac confirmativum Apostolicum, quod Communionem cum Diabolis foventes (quale quid in omnes impios cadere Apostolus Johannes testatur 1. Ep. 1, 6. cap. 3. vers. 6. 8. 9.) omni communionis cum Christo possibilitate excludit 1. Cor. 10, 21. Non potestis poculum Domini bibere & poculum dæmoniorum. Non potestis Mensæ Domini participes fieri, & mensæ dæmoniorum.

lemmas.gloss: cup of the Lord … cup of demons
